Outboard won't start, stalls, or runs rough: mobile diagnosis and repair

No start, dies at idle, alarm beeping, loss of power, overheating, won't shift. A mechanic comes to the boat with a scan tool and the common parts, finds the cause, and quotes the fix on the spot.

What's included

  • Computer scan for fault codes and engine history
  • Fuel pressure and fuel quality check
  • Spark, compression, and timing checks as needed
  • Cooling system and overheat alarm diagnosis
  • Written quote before repair
  • Repair on the same visit when parts are on the truck
When

As soon as it misbehaves. Running an outboard with an overheat or oil alarm turns a $400 fix into a powerhead.

Time on site

1 to 2 hours to diagnose; repair time varies

What it usually costs here

$100 to $150 diagnostic or trip fee, usually credited toward the repair. Most no-start and rough-running repairs land between $300 and $900.

In Tampa Bay specifically

Boats that sat through summer in Apollo Beach and Ruskin canals come back with varnished fuel and stuck injectors. Boats that live on lifts near the Gulf in Tarpon Springs and Dunedin see more corrosion-related electrical no-starts.

Engines

YamahaMercurySuzukiHonda MarineTohatsuEvinrude and Johnson

Questions we get

My engine starts but dies when I put it in gear. What is it?

Often a fuel delivery problem (clogged filter, weak low-pressure pump, bad fuel) or an idle air issue. Sometimes the shift interrupt switch. The scan tool and a fuel pressure test narrow it in minutes.

The overheat alarm goes off after 20 minutes at speed.

Classic water pump impeller or thermostat, sometimes a blocked pickup from barnacles. Do not keep running it. This is one of the most common calls in Tampa Bay.

Can you fix it at the ramp or on the water?

At the ramp or dock, yes. On the water, no; we can help you arrange a tow.
